clue.text: Hearing perhaps about us quietly creates tension

indicators.note: about tells us the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: hearing is one example of a sense
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone muttering about us in a courtroom hearing leaves everyone on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a court session; 'perhaps' shows it is just one of the five senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the state of anxious uncertainty that a story builds up, a form of nervous strain.

clue.text: You love wriggling in sister's grip

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within another
grip says the outer piece holds the other firmly inside

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for sister

indicators.note: wriggling means twisting about, so these letters squirm into a new order

explanation.surface: A sibling hugs you lovingly while you squirm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' is the person doing this crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: The reader of the clue is the person cracking the puzzle, a playful self-reference.

clue.text: Put an end to urge for food

parts.note: to scotch a rumour or plan is to stop it
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: Stopping one's cravings for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scotch egg is a British snack: a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a savoury snack, an example of something to eat.

clue.text: Long head of hair raises our charm

indicators.note: raises means lifts up, and in a down entry that reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a mane is a long, thick head of hair

explanation.surface: Long flowing hair lifts our spirits and captivates us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like a verb meaning yearn, but belongs to the description of the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to captivate or win the love of someone, which is to charm them.

clue.text: So — nothing's cleared off? Lazy creep!

indicators.note: cleared off means removed or gone away, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: O is the round figure nought, nothing
idle means lazy

explanation.surface: An exasperated person asks whether the idler has done nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to move furtively or sideways, much as one would creep.

clue.text: Where people study page penned by novelist

indicators.note: penned by means held inside, as in a pen, so the novelist's name encloses the page letter

parts.note: Albert Camus, French author of The Outsider

explanation.surface: A single page written by a famous author, presumably studied at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a university, where students go to learn.

clue.text: Unfavourable notice on poet's output

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a poet writes verse

explanation.surface: A bad review appears for a poet's latest work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' suggests a critic's review, but it is an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions or comments are hostile or harmful, the same as unfavourable.

clue.text: Slug alcoholic drink

definitions.meaning: to slug someone is to hit them hard
a mixed drink of spirits, fruit and spice served from a bowl

explanation.surface: Knocking back a strong drink in one swig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slug' suggests a gulp of liquor, but it means to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is a hard blow, and a party bowl of spiced alcohol has the same name.

clue.text: Small fish: they're often found at sea

definitions.meaning: a skipper is a small leaping fish such as the saury
ship captains spend their working lives on the water

explanation.surface: Little fish are often seen out in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Both readings seem to be about fish; the second is really about ship captains.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small jumping fish and the captain in charge of a boat.

clue.text: Moved along cave and dislodged diamonds

indicators.note: dislodged means knocked out of place, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: Explorers moved through a cave and prised gems loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to go forward, so the past tense means moved on or forwards.

clue.text: Sculptor left advice on a Rodin bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so these letters are smashed and remade

explanation.surface: An artist gives guidance on a bust by Rodin, the French sculptor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a sculpture to go with Rodin, but it is the anagram signal for ADVICE ON A RODIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance polymath also made sculpture, notably a famous unfinished horse statue, so he is one example.

clue.text: Shut in linen closet with no fabric around

indicators.note: with no tells us letters are taken away from the words before
around says the removed letters sit on both sides of what is left

parts.note: taken as written; the clue frames this as stripping a fabric from round the words, so the run of letters inside is a coincidence of that deletion rather than a signalled hiding
lint is a soft fabric used for dressing wounds

explanation.surface: A linen cupboard holding nothing made of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing L-I-N from the front and T from the back of LINEN CLOSET, as 'with no' and 'around' direct, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose something is to surround it so that it is confined within.

clue.text: Shows trendy method of transport

parts.note: airs, as a verb, means displays or shows
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a fashionable way of getting about.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible or blimp carries passengers through the air, so it is a means of travel.

clue.text: Obsessive about following organised routine

indicators.note: following puts the abbreviation after the reworked letters
organised means arranged into order, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

parts.note: C, circa, is the Latin abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: An obsessive person sticks to a strictly ordered daily routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone neurotic is anxious and fixated, which overlaps with being obsessive.

clue.text: Ideas, however terrible, suffice at first

parts.note: though can mean however, at the end of a sentence

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Any ideas, however bad, will do to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts and ideas are both products of thinking: plain synonyms.

clue.text: Duck's sign of hesitation about fish

indicators.note: about says the hesitation goes round the fish

parts.note: er is the sound a hesitant speaker makes
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A duck hesitates over a fish it might eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck, famous for its soft down.

clue.text: Hairy bug found in party by American

indicators.note: by means beside, so the last piece goes next to the rest
found in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a do is a party
to bug someone is to annoy, or anger, them

explanation.surface: A furry insect turns up at an American's party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' and 'bug' paint a furry insect, but hairy is slang for risky and bug is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a hairy situation is a frightening, risky one.

clue.text: Carp and eels — unusual substitutes

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters take an unexpected arrangement

explanation.surface: Carp and eels make odd replacements for one another in a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace something is to put something else in its place, which is what one substitutes.

clue.text: Skirts editor agrees oddly to be removed

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word are dropped, keeping only the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A fashion editor agrees that skirts should be taken off the pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Skirts here is a verb or plural noun meaning borders, not the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirts as a noun can mean outer margins or borders, which are the edges of something.

clue.text: Mixed cooler wine

parts.note: cooler and stir are both slang for prison
red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: A blend of wines, one of them chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' suggests a wine chiller, but it is slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred describes ingredients that have been combined by moving a spoon through them.

clue.text: Instructing crowd leaving hospital to call

indicators.note: leaving means going out of, so the letter departs from the crowd

parts.note: a horde is a large crowd
H is the abbreviation for hospital, seen on road signs
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: Telling a crowd to leave the hospital and phone someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering someone means giving them commands, which is instructing them.

clue.text: Gold back and large — Liberal with first-class type of desk

indicators.note: back means reversed, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
top means first-rate

explanation.surface: A politician's grand gilded antique writing desk.
explanation.definitionFit: This writing desk has a flexible slatted cover that slides up and over.

clue.text: Sermon half-abandoned following drink problem

indicators.note: following places the remaining piece after the drink

parts.note: tea is a drink

indicators.note: half-abandoned means dropping the second half of the word

explanation.surface: A preacher gives up halfway through, troubled by the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzle or tricky question, so a brainteaser is a problem.

clue.text: Watching throne — and who sits on it?

parts.note: throne is jocular slang for the lavatory, the loo
a monarch sits on a throne

explanation.surface: Seeing a throne and wondering whose seat it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The throne is first the toilet, then the royal seat whose occupant is a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking and watching both mean directing one's eyes at something.

clue.text: Big cat — and what it might do? Not initially

indicators.note: not initially means without the first letter

parts.note: a big cat may leap on its prey: pounce

explanation.surface: A large feline and its likely next move.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called by this name, so it is one of the large wild felines.

clue.text: Pass by student, for example, and Head of English here?

definitions.text: Pass by student, for example, and Head of English here?

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
L, for learner, stands for a student

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A student passing an academic in charge of the English department.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the place: students, and a head of English, are found there.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is a place of higher education with students and heads of department.

clue.text: Parcel looks somewhat … It needs a bow!

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wrapped package that seems to want a ribbon tied on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a stringed instrument played by drawing a bow across its strings.

clue.text: Drag consultation out? No Democrat gets kudos

indicators.note: out means put out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
no says this letter is to be absent from the words

explanation.surface: A politician earns praise for not dragging out a consultation.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise or credit, and expressions of praise for success are the same thing.

clue.text: Tears from papa, squashed by stones

indicators.note: squashed by means pressed in between, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: fruit stones are seeds
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A father weeps after being crushed by stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' reads as crying, but it is the verb, rhyming with bears: rushes along.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear along is to go very fast, so tears means races or hurries.

clue.text: Gibbons perhaps turn up tailless and sit by river

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to come is to turn up or arrive
to pose is to sit for a portrait

explanation.surface: Apes appear minus their tails and sit beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibbons are not apes here: Orlando Gibbons was an English Renaissance writer of church music.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando Gibbons wrote madrigals and anthems, an example of a music writer.
